Looking at this question, I need to recall the structural biology of the Csx23 (Csx) response regulator from *Vibrio cholerae* and its interaction with cyclic tetra-adenylate (c-AMP4, or pppA4).

Csx is a hybrid histidine kinase/response regulator that serves as the receptor for cyclic tetra-adenylate in the osmoregulatory signaling pathway of *V. cholerae*. Crystal structure studies of the Csx-c-AMP4 complex have identified the metal ions involved in coordinating the ligand binding.

In the crystal structure of Csx bound to c-AMP4, potassium (K⁺) ions were identified as the metal ions that coordinate and stabilize the cyclic tetra-adenylate in the binding pocket of Csx23.

[ANSWER]C[/ANSWER]
